mainTopic: How much kosher food is needed to cancel forbidden food: eggs, fat in a pot, and the rule of sixty or one hundred.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: only an egg with an אפרוח (chick) inside gives flavor to food, not an egg from a טמאה bird. A ברייתא seems to say otherwise, and the גמרא reads it so that the 'טמאה' egg is really a kosher bird's egg with a chick inside. Next come two stories about forbidden fat falling into a pot of meat. They teach that you cannot count the pot's absorbed kosher meat, and that a half-olive still needs the full sixty, since חצי שיעור אסור מן התורה. The גמרא then asks how many kosher eggs cancel one forbidden egg. רב הונא makes clear that sixty-one are needed besides the forbidden egg. Stories about the sons of רבי show rulings below sixty, and רבי חייא's 'Is there even thirty?' is explained as only an exaggeration. Finally, בר קפרא's rule is quoted as 'all Torah prohibitions are cancelled in sixty' and also as 'in one hundred'. The גמרא says both numbers come from the נזיר's cooked foreleg, and the ברייתא explaining this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only an egg with a chick gives flavor
steps.stepSummary: The answer from before is completed: the flavor rule is about an egg with a chick inside, not about an egg of a non-kosher bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule is about an egg with a chick in it. But a non-kosher egg does not give flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The text picks up in the middle of an answer from just before. It limits the rule of an egg giving flavor to a בֵּיצַת אֶפְרוֹחַ, and says a טמאה egg is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that a chick inside an egg has real meat flavor that spreads into the food. A plain egg from a non-kosher bird is said not to give flavor in the same way. This claim is the target of the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg with a chick (an embryo) developing inside it.
A chick.
Here: an egg from a non-kosher bird.

phrases.english: With an egg that contains a chick,
but a non-kosher egg – not.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּבֵיצַת אֶפְרוֹחַ, אֲבָל טְמֵאָה – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg with a chick gives flavor, but an egg of a non-kosher bird does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows non-kosher eggs do give flavor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says kosher eggs boiled with non-kosher eggs are all forbidden if there is enough to give flavor. This suggests non-kosher eggs do give flavor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: kosher eggs that were boiled with non-kosher eggs are all forbidden if there is enough to give flavor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 1 using a ברייתא about kosher and טמאות eggs boiled together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said a non-kosher egg gives no flavor. This ברייתא says non-kosher eggs can make kosher eggs forbidden through נותן טעם. That would mean non-kosher eggs do have flavor, which seems to contradict step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher eggs.
He boiled them.
Giving flavor; when there is enough forbidden food to flavor the mixture.
All of them are forbidden.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Kosher eggs that one boiled
with non-kosher eggs,
if there is enough in them to impart flavor –
they are all forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a non-kosher egg does not give flavor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids kosher eggs because of non-kosher eggs through נותן טעם, so non-kosher eggs must give flavor.

steps.title: In the ברייתא, 'non-kosher' means an egg with a chick
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is also talking about an egg with a chick. It calls that egg 'טמאה' because the chick makes it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too it means an egg with a chick. Why does it call it 'non-kosher'? Since it has a chick inside, it calls it 'non-kosher.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer re-reads the ברייתא so it fits step 1. The 'non-kosher eggs' there are really kosher-bird eggs with chicks inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word טמאה usually means an egg from a non-kosher bird. Here it is read as 'a forbidden egg,' because the chick inside makes it forbidden to eat. Read this way, the ברייתא no longer proves that a plain non-kosher egg gives flavor.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too.
Why?
It calls it.
Since; because.

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'טמאה' does not mean the egg comes from a non-kosher bird. It means a kosher bird's egg that became forbidden because a chick is inside.

phrases.english: Here too, it is about an egg with a chick,
And why does it call it 'non-kosher'?
Since it has a chick inside it,
it calls it 'non-kosher.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי בְּבֵיצַת אֶפְרוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'טמאות' means eggs from non-kosher birds, which would show they give flavor.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'טמאות' means eggs with chicks, which are forbidden, so the ברייתא fits step 1.

steps.title: The סיפא shows the רישא is about an egg without a chick
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא talks separately about a chick found in one egg. So the beginning must be about eggs without chicks.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the ברייתא teaches: eggs that were boiled and a chick was found in one of them are all forbidden if there is enough to give flavor. This shows that the beginning is about an egg without a chick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 3, using the next part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the סיפא is about an egg with a chick, it looks like a new case. Then the רישא should be a different case: real non-kosher eggs without chicks. That brings back the challenge from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching.
The first part of a teaching.
From this it follows; we can infer.
We are dealing with.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
Eggs that one boiled
and a chick was found in one of them,
if there is enough in them to impart flavor –
they are all forbidden,
it follows that in the first clause
we are dealing with one that has no chick in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'טמאות' in the רישא means eggs with chicks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא already covers the case of a chick, so the רישא must be a different case: eggs without chicks.

steps.title: The סיפא explains the רישא
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא is not a separate case. It explains how the רישא happens: a chick was found in one of the eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining: kosher eggs boiled with non-kosher eggs are all forbidden if there is enough to give flavor. How? For example, one boiled them and a chick was found in one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the סיפא is an explanation of the רישא. So both parts talk about an egg with a chick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 assumed the סיפא was a new case. Here the סיפא is read as 'how so?', which describes the case of the רישא. That keeps the answer of step 3, and with it the rule of step 1, that a plain non-kosher egg does not give flavor.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining; the later part explains the earlier part.
How so?
For example; such as.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is one case: kosher eggs boiled together, with a chick found in one of them. The egg with the chick is the 'טמאה' egg. So the ברייתא does not prove that an egg from a non-kosher bird gives flavor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. A later clause that seems to be a new case can be read as explaining the earlier clause.

phrases.english: It is explaining:
phrases.notes: The סיפא isn't a new case; it tells us what the first part was talking about.

phrases.english: Kosher eggs that one boiled
with non-kosher eggs,
if there is enough in them to impart flavor –
they are all forbidden.
How so?
For example, where one boiled them
and a chick was found in one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּירוּשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the סיפא as an explanation of the רישא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is a separate case, so the רישא is about eggs without chicks.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא explains the רישא, so both are about an egg with a chick.

steps.title: Proof that the first part of the ברייתא is about an egg with a chick
steps.stepSummary: If the רישא were about an egg without a chick, the סיפא about a chick would be pointless. So the רישא must also be about a chick.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you thought the first part was about an egg with no chick, then the second part would be obvious. If an egg with no chick already forbids the others, do we even need to say that an egg with a chick does?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings logical support for the answer it just gave in step 5: the ברייתא is talking about an egg with a chick inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the רישא forbids the other eggs even when there is no chick. Then a case with a chick, which is more forbidden, would surely forbid them too. The סיפא would teach nothing new. To avoid an extra, useless clause, the רישא must also be about a chick.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense: logical support for the last answer
The first part of the ברייתא
A chick that has started forming inside the egg
Is it even necessary to say? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if it would enter your mind
that the first part is where there is no chick in it,
now, if where there is no chick it is forbidden,
is it necessary to say so where there is a chick?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 5 with logic from how the ברייתא is built
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the רישא of the ברייתא is about an egg with a chick
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that a clause in a ברייתא should not be useless: if the רישא had no chick, the סיפא would be obvious

steps.title: The proof fails: the second part could be explaining the first part
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא may have been taught to show that the רישא is about an egg without a chick, and even so the other eggs are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is your reason, it proves nothing. The תנא taught the second part to make the first part clear. Without it, you might think the first part is about an egg with a chick, and that without a chick the eggs are permitted. So he taught the second part about a chick. From this we learn that the first part is about no chick, and even so the eggs are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 6. The 'extra' סיפא has a real job after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא is not useless. Because it names the chick case on its own, it tells us the רישא is a different case, one with no chick. So the extra clause can be read the other way, and the proof does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: That is no proof; the argument does not hold
The last part of the ברייתא
To reveal or make clear
Permitted
By inference; from this it follows

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not settle the question. It only shows that the proof in step 6 is not convincing. The answer from step 5 can still stand. It just has no extra support from this logic.

phrases.english: If it is because of this, it is no proof:
he taught the last part to reveal the meaning of the first part,
so that you should not say:
the first part is where there is a chick in it,
but where there is no chick, it is permitted.
So he taught the last part as where there is a chick,
from which it follows that the first part is where there is no chick,
and even so it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם הָא לָא אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the supporting proof of step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the supporting proof of step 6, not the answer of step 5 itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא is not useless. It can serve to show that the רישא is about an egg without a chick.

steps.title: Forbidden fat in a pot of meat: רב אסי wants to count what the pot absorbed
steps.stepSummary: An olive-size of forbidden fat fell into a pot of kosher meat. רב אסי wanted to include the meat absorbed in the pot walls when checking for sixty times the fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: An olive-size of forbidden fat fell into a pot of meat. רב אסי thought to measure it together with what the pot had absorbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a practical story about cancelling out forbidden fat in kosher meat. This step sets up the case, and the next step challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidden food is cancelled when there is enough permitted food against it. רב אסי wanted to count the meat soaked into the pot walls as part of the permitted amount, which would make it easier to reach the needed ratio.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-size, a basic halachic measure
Forbidden fat (חֵלֶב)
A pot
To measure it, to work out whether there is enough to cancel it
Absorbed

phrases.english: There was a certain olive-size of forbidden fat
that fell into a pot of meat.
Rav Asi thought to measure it
including what the pot had absorbed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא כְּזֵיתָא תַּרְבָּא דִּנְפַל בְּדִיקּוּלָא דְּבִשְׂרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: from eggs to the measure for cancelling forbidden fat in meat
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אסי proposed counting the pot's absorbed meat toward the permitted amount

steps.title: The pot absorbs the forbidden fat too
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן object: if the pot absorbed kosher meat, it also absorbed forbidden fat, so you cannot count only the kosher part.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב אשי: Is that to say the pot absorbed the permitted meat but did not absorb the forbidden fat?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge the plan from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pot walls soak up whatever is cooking, both the kosher meat and the forbidden fat. Adding only the kosher part to the count is one-sided. The absorbed forbidden fat would have to be counted too, so nothing is gained.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a challenging question)
The permitted food
The forbidden food

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Ashi:
phrases.notes: The story began with רב אסי, but here it says רב אשי. Some versions say רב אשי both times.

phrases.english: Is that to say it absorbed the permitted food,
but did not absorb the forbidden food?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אַטּוּ דְּהֶיתֵּרָא בָּלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and rejects the measuring method of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to count the pot's absorbed meat toward the permitted amount
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pot absorbs forbidden food as well as permitted food, so counting only the permitted part is inconsistent

steps.title: A half-olive of fat: מר בר רב אשי wants to use only thirty half-olives
steps.stepSummary: A half-olive of forbidden fat fell into a pot of meat. מר בר רב אשי thought thirty half-olives of meat would be enough to cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A half-olive of forbidden fat fell into a pot of meat. מר בר רב אשי thought to measure it with thirty half-olives.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, similar story is told. This step sets up the case, and the next steps show why his father rejected it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual measure is sixty times the forbidden food. מר בר רב אשי wanted to use only thirty, half the ratio. This suggests he treated a half-olive as less serious than a full olive.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of an olive-size
Thirty

phrases.english: There was a certain half-olive-size of forbidden fat
that fell into a pot of meat.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי לְשַׁעוֹרֵיהּ
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi thought to measure it
with thirty half-olive-sizes.
phrases.notes: That is half the usual sixty-to-one ratio.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא פַּלְגָא דְּזֵיתָא דְּתַרְבָּא דִּנְפַל בְּדִיקּוּלָא דְּבִשְׂרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story on the same theme of measuring ביטול
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר בר רב אשי proposed cancelling a half-olive in thirty half-olives instead of sixty

steps.title: רב אשי: do not take rabbinic measures lightly
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rebukes his son. Even rabbinic measures like the sixty ratio must be kept carefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father said to him: Didn't I tell you not to treat the measures of the רבנן lightly?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects his son's plan from step 10 with a first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sixty ratio is a measure set by the רבנן. Cutting it in half because the case seems minor is treating it lightly, and רב אשי says that is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not treat lightly or belittle
Measures set by the רבנן

phrases.english: His father said to him:
Didn't I tell you:
do not treat the measures of the Rabbis lightly?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמֵינָא לָךְ לָא תְּזַלְזֵל בְּשִׁיעוּרִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the plan of step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposal to use thirty instead of sixty
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It treats a rabbinic measure lightly

steps.title: Second reason: a half-measure is forbidden מן התורה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that according to רבי יוחנן, a חצי שיעור is forbidden by the תורה, so a half-olive is not a lighter case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, didn't רבי יוחנן say that a half-measure is forbidden by the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second reason why his son's leniency is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His son's idea assumed a half-olive is a weaker prohibition. But רבי יוחנן says even less than the full measure is forbidden מן התורה. So the half-olive is a real prohibition and needs the full sixty-to-one ratio.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the full measure (here, less than an olive-size)
Forbidden by the תורה itself, not only by the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: Two rules for ביטול: (1) a pot absorbs forbidden and permitted food alike, so you cannot add only its absorbed kosher part; (2) a half-olive of forbidden food still needs the full sixty, because a חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה and rabbinic measures must not be cut.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule חצי שיעור אסור מן התורה is a major principle that comes up all across ש״ס.

phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
A half-measure is forbidden by the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חֲצִי שִׁיעוּר אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger reason to the rejection in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that a half-olive is a lighter prohibition
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה, so it needs the full ratio

steps.title: One forbidden egg is canceled at sixty-one
steps.stepSummary: Through a long chain of teachers, רב שמן בר אבא reports that the house of the נשיא ruled that a forbidden egg in sixty eggs is forbidden, but in sixty-one it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said, in the name of a long chain of teachers going back to an elder named רבי יעקב, that the house of the נשיא said: if one forbidden egg is mixed in, at sixty the mixture is forbidden, and at sixty-one it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how many kosher eggs are needed to cancel one forbidden egg. A long chain of teachers passes down the rule 'sixty is forbidden, sixty-one is permitted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular forbidden food is canceled at sixty, but here an egg needs more than sixty. The wording leaves it unclear whether the sixty-one includes the forbidden egg. This unclear point drives the rest of the section.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg; here, a forbidden egg mixed in with kosher eggs
In sixty, meaning when there are sixty eggs
Forbidden
Permitted
The house (court) of the נשיא, the head of the Jewish community

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אִידִי בַּר גֵּרְשֹׁם,
phrases.english: that Rav Idi bar Idi bar Gershom said
that Levi bar Perata said
that Rabbi Nachum said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּירְיָים מִשּׁוּם זָקֵן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Biryam said in the name of a certain elder
and his name was Rabbi Yaakov
that the house of the Nasi said:
An egg in sixty is forbidden
phrases.notes: He means one forbidden egg mixed in with kosher eggs, sixty eggs in all.

phrases.english: in sixty-one, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אִידִי בַּר גֵּרְשֹׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from canceling forbidden fat in a pot (steps 8-12) to a new case of canceling a forbidden egg.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forbidden egg is not canceled at sixty but is canceled at sixty-one.

steps.title: רבי זירא says the wording sets a new permitted limit
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא warns רב שמן בר אבא that his words set a clear line for permitting, even though the two greatest sages of the generation, quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי, used the same words without explaining this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב שמן בר אבא: Notice that you are setting a clear limit for permitting, while the two greatest sages of the generation did not explain this. רבי יעקב בר אידי and רבי שמואל בר נחמני both said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: an egg in sixty is forbidden, in sixty-one it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא reacts to רב שמן's teaching. He says it sounds like a clear ruling on something the great sages left unexplained, and he sets up the next step by quoting their version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's version uses the exact same words as רב שמן's chain. Since it was never explained whether 'sixty-one' counts the forbidden egg, רבי זירא is surprised that רב שמן speaks as if the answer is known. It is a challenge: how can you be so sure?

keyTerms.meaning: A limit for permitting, a clear line where the mixture becomes allowed
The great sages of the generation
They did not explain or make clear
Both of them

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Shemen bar Abba:

phrases.aramaic: רְאֵה שֶׁאַתָּה מֵטִיל בָּהּ גְּבוּל הֶיתֵּר,
phrases.english: See that you are setting a limit of permission in it
phrases.notes: He means that from your words, it sounds like sixty-one in total, counting the forbidden egg, is enough.

phrases.english: for the two great sages of the generation
did not make the matter clear.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: both of them said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
An egg in sixty is forbidden
in sixty-one, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְאֵה שֶׁאַתָּה מֵטִיל בָּהּ גְּבוּל הֶיתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how definite רב שמן's teaching from step 13 really is.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שמן's implied claim that sixty-one in total, counting the forbidden egg, is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The great sages taught the same words in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי and never made clear what they meant, so רב שמן cannot treat the meaning as settled.

steps.title: Does sixty-one include the forbidden egg?
steps.stepSummary: The sages asked whether 'sixty-one' means sixty-one counting the forbidden egg or sixty-one besides it. They did not resolve it, yet רב שמן seems to have resolved it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: sixty-one together with the forbidden egg, or perhaps sixty-one not counting it? They did not resolve it, and you, Master, resolve it simply.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא spells out the question: does the count of sixty-one include the forbidden egg? He adds that the great sages did not resolve it, yet רב שמן speaks as if it is simple. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two choices are sixty kosher eggs plus one forbidden egg, or sixty-one kosher eggs plus the forbidden one. רבי יהושע בן לוי's students never decided. רב שמן's version seems to choose the easier side, and רבי זירא points out the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked by them, an open question
Together with it, counting the forbidden egg
Apart from it, not counting the forbidden egg
And they did not resolve it
Master, a polite way of saying 'you'

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the number sixty-one. The only question is whether the forbidden egg itself is one of the sixty-one, which makes a difference of one egg.

phrases.english: And they asked: in sixty-one,
does that count the forbidden egg
or perhaps it means not counting it?
And they did not resolve it,
and you, Master, simply resolve it!
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is still talking to רב שמן. His version made it sound like the forbidden egg counts in the sixty-one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בְּשִׁשִּׁים וְאַחַת, בַּהֲדֵי דִּידַהּ, אוֹ דִילְמָא לְבַר מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the unclear point behind רבי זירא's challenge in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'sixty-one' includes the forbidden egg or means sixty-one kosher eggs besides it.

steps.title: רב הונא: sixty-one besides the forbidden egg
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's version clearly says sixty kosher eggs plus the forbidden one is forbidden, and sixty-one plus the forbidden one is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: an egg in sixty plus the forbidden egg is forbidden; in sixty-one plus the forbidden egg, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a version of the rule from רב הונא that answers the open question. The forbidden egg is not counted in the sixty-one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added word 'והיא' (and it) shows that the forbidden egg is counted on top of the number. So sixty kosher eggs plus the forbidden one is still forbidden, and only sixty-one kosher eggs plus the forbidden one is permitted. This is the stricter side of the question in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: And it, meaning the forbidden egg is added on top of the number

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, a forbidden egg is canceled only when there are sixty-one kosher eggs besides it, sixty-two eggs in all.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב הונא's wording, with the added 'והיא,' answers the question from step 15 on the stricter side: the forbidden egg is not one of the sixty-one.

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
An egg in sixty plus it is forbidden
phrases.notes: "Plus it" means the forbidden egg is counted separately, on top of the sixty kosher eggs.

phrases.english: in sixty-one plus it, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open question of step 15 by making clear that the forbidden egg is not counted.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sixty-one kosher eggs are needed besides the forbidden egg.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A forbidden egg is canceled only by sixty-one kosher eggs besides it.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל permits with forty-five
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל ברבי rules on a mixture brought to him. He says his father did not require sixty and permitted with forty-seven, and he himself will permit with forty-five.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone came before רבן גמליאל ברבי with a mixture. He said: My father did not require sixty; he permitted with forty-seven. I will permit with forty-five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story of a ruling that permitted a mixture even though there was not sixty times as much kosher food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the measure was sixty. Here a son of רבי says his father permitted with only forty-seven, and he goes even lower, to forty-five. The story shows that in some cases these sages were lenient below sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: measured, set the required amount
I will measure, I will set the amount
sixty, the usual amount of kosher food needed to cancel forbidden food
forty-seven

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'my father did not measure forty-seven' as 'my father did not allow forty-seven.' It means: he did not demand sixty; forty-seven was enough for him.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: A certain person who came before Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, so this is his son.

phrases.english: He said to him: My father did not measure [sixty]
phrases.notes: The word 'sixty' is not written, but it is meant: my father did not insist on the full sixty.

phrases.english: [he permitted] with forty-seven
and I will measure with forty-five.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rule of sixty and sixty-one, the גמרא brings practical rulings that went below sixty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל ברבי permits a mixture with forty-five times kosher food, going lower than his father's forty-seven.

steps.title: רבי שמעון permits with forty-three
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון ברבי tells a similar story: his father permitted with forty-five, and he will permit with forty-three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone came before רבי שמעון ברבי. He said: My father did not require sixty; he permitted with forty-five. I will permit with forty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, matching story: another son of רבי permits a mixture with even less kosher food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats. רבי שמעון quotes his father as permitting with forty-five, and he goes two lower, to forty-three. The numbers differ from the first story, but the idea is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: forty-five
forty-three
a certain person who came before (a sage with a question)

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: A certain person who came before Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi
He said to him: My father did not measure [sixty]
[he permitted] with forty-five
and I will measure with forty-three.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 17, with slightly lower numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון ברבי permits a mixture with forty-three times kosher food.

steps.title: רבי חייא asks: Is there even thirty?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא forbids a mixture, telling the questioner there is not even thirty times as much kosher food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone came before רבי חייא with a mixture. He said to him: Is there even thirty?
steps.whatsHappening: A third story: רבי חייא rejects a mixture by asking, 'Is there even thirty?' This sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's words suggest the mixture fails badly, since it does not even reach thirty. But the way he said it raises a puzzle about what would happen if there were thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: is there at all? (used in a question that expects 'no')
thirty

phrases.english: A certain person who came before Rabbi Chiya
He said to him: Is there even thirty?
phrases.notes: He means thirty times as much kosher food as forbidden food. Since there isn't, the mixture is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third case story, this time one where the mixture was forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא forbids a mixture that does not have even thirty times kosher food.

steps.title: Does that mean thirty would be enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי חייא's words that thirty might be enough to permit, which goes against the rule of sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it was forbidden is that there was not thirty. So if there were thirty, would we permit it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבי חייא's words closely and finds a problem: they seem to say that thirty would be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only reason for forbidding was 'there is not thirty,' then with thirty it should be permitted. But the rule is sixty, so this reading clashes with it. The גמרא wants to know what רבי חייא really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason (is only because...)
but then, it follows that
there is not / there is
we measure by it, we go by it and permit

phrases.english: The reason is that there is not thirty
but if there is thirty, do we measure by it [and permit]?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֵיכָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים, הָא אִיכָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים מְשַׁעֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי חייא in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's statement 'Is there even thirty?'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By implication, his words suggest thirty would permit the mixture, which goes against the rule of sixty.

steps.title: It was only an exaggeration
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that רבי חייא was exaggerating. He was not setting thirty as a rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: It was an exaggeration.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question: רבי חייא's 'thirty' was just a way of speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא was saying the mixture is so far off that it does not even reach thirty, never mind sixty. So we may not learn from his words that thirty is enough. The rule of sixty stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: an exaggeration, an overstatement

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא's 'Is there even thirty?' is only an exaggeration, not a new rule. Sixty remains the measure, even though some sons of רבי permitted somewhat less in their own rulings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: It was an exaggeration.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: גּוּזְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording as an exaggeration, not a legal limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא meant that thirty times kosher food would permit the mixture.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא was only stressing how small the kosher amount was; thirty is not a legal limit.

steps.title: All Torah prohibitions are cancelled in sixty
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports, through רבי יהושע בן לוי, that בר קפרא said all forbidden foods of the תורה are cancelled when mixed into sixty times as much kosher food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יהושע בן לוי said in the name of בר קפרא: all forbidden foods in the תורה are cancelled in sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a general rule: any forbidden food mixed into sixty times its amount of kosher food is cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw sages ruling case by case, sometimes with less than sixty. Here we get one broad rule that covers every food prohibition in the תורה, not just one specific case. It comes through a chain of three rabbis, which will matter in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The forbidden foods of the תורה
In sixty: cancelled when there is sixty times as much kosher food
In the name of: quoting an earlier sage

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the well-known rule of ביטול בשישים that is used in practical כשרות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara:
All the prohibitions in the Torah are in sixty.
phrases.notes: He means they are cancelled when mixed into sixty times as much permitted food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from individual stories about mixtures to a general rule for all prohibitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All forbidden foods of the תורה are cancelled in sixty times their amount.

steps.title: A student reports the same chain said one hundred
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק challenges his teacher: through רב אסי he heard the same rabbis quoted as saying all prohibitions are cancelled in one hundred, not sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said before him: My teacher, you say this? רב אסי said, quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי in the name of בר קפרא: all prohibitions in the תורה are cancelled in one hundred!
steps.whatsHappening: A student pushes back on his teacher's quote, saying he heard the same chain of rabbis give a different number, one hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not about logic but about what בר קפרא actually said. Both reports go back to the same people, רבי יהושע בן לוי and בר קפרא, yet one says sixty and the other says one hundred. The next step shows that both numbers were learned from the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Said before him: a student speaking respectfully to his teacher
You say this? A surprised challenge
In one hundred: cancelled with a hundred times as much kosher food

steps.confusionAlert: Both quotes go back to the very same rabbis, רבי יהושע בן לוי and בר קפרא. The only difference is who passed it on (רבי חייא בר אבא or רב אסי) and the number.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said before him:
My teacher, you say this?
This is what Rav Asi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara:
All the prohibitions in the Torah are in one hundred!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי, אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן? הָכִי אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the accuracy of the quote in step 22 with a conflicting version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that בר קפרא said all prohibitions are cancelled in sixty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different line of transmission from the same original rabbis gives the number one hundred, so the sixty report seems wrong.

steps.title: Both numbers come from the cooked foreleg
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both versions, sixty and one hundred, were learned from the נזיר's cooked foreleg (זרוע בשלה). It begins quoting a ברייתא on that פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned it only from the 'cooked foreleg,' as it is written: 'And the כהן shall take the cooked foreleg...' And a ברייתא teaches: 'Cooked'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the shared source for both numbers: the cooked foreleg of the נזיר's ram. It is setting up a ברייתא that will explain how that פסוק teaches cancellation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of choosing one report, the גמרא shows that both come from the same פסוק. So the disagreement is about how to measure using that source, not about where the rule comes from. The explanation is in the ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The cooked foreleg of the נזיר's ram, given to the כהן
They learned it: they derived the rule
As it is written: introduces a פסוק
Etc.: the פסוק continues

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties both numbers for ביטול to one פסוק in the תורה. The ברייתא that explains how is on the next amud.

phrases.english: And both of them learned it
only from the 'cooked foreleg,'
as it is written: 'And the priest shall take'
the cooked foreleg, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:19, about the ram a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות.

phrases.english: And a baraita teaches: 'Cooked'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מִזְּרוֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the two conflicting numbers from steps 22 and 23 share one source in the תורה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that forbidden food can be cancelled in a mixture, in both the sixty and hundred versions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The cooked foreleg of the נזיר's ram (במדבר 6:19), explained by a ברייתא.
